moment: the engine reports itself — the numbers the in-app performance panel draws
source: JOS-483 (owner ruling 19 surface: "the performance chip should incl perf of the server in end state"; not a plan-doc moment — the four numbered moments are 01-04)
note: THE OWNER'S ASK, ON THE WIRE: `i want to see the server in the cpu/performance overlay in app`. Four answers are worked here and they are four different sentences. The FIRST is a launched engine with nothing attached: `idle`, a real uptime, an empty `serve` list, and an `ingest` with no field in it at all — ABSENT, never zero, because a `scanMs` of 0 would say a whole log folded instantly rather than that no scan has finished. The SECOND is the same engine mid-scan with a subscription already open: the ingest has measured its spell catalog but not its scan, and the serve row is every counter at a REAL zero beside `subscribers: 1` — a window that is watching and has been served nothing yet, which is precisely the state a person stares at when a view looks empty and which an omitted row would make indistinguishable from a view nobody opened. Its two latency fields are absent, because nothing was timed. The THIRD is that session gone live: the ingest half is complete and the serve table carries the two measurements ruling 19 names — the payload budget (bytes, and the widest single frame) and fold-to-frame latency in MICROSECONDS, because cutting a fifty-row window off a fold takes tens of them and a serve path reporting `0 ms` reads as a measurement nobody took. The FOURTH is the op's only refusal: a fold that had a door and did not answer through it. An engine with nothing attached is NOT this — it is the first answer — and the distinction is the whole reason a wedged ingest is worth saying out loud rather than drawing as a row of zeros.

error.message: the fold did not answer within 5000 ms
